title: Selector Composition IR
description: Serializable intermediate representation for the Mishmash Selector (C2). Every composition run is expressed as one instance of this schema: which sources contributed, what the user asked for per axis, what must hold after composition, how competing claims were arbitrated, where every emitted element came from, and the axes three variants must structurally differ along.

sourceSlots.description: One entry per reference the user supplied. Each source slot pins an id, the breakpoints captured for it, and the evidence pointers (DOM path + breakpoint) available to ground directives and provenance against it.

evidencePointers.description: Compact '<domPath>@<breakpoint>' strings -- one per (domPath, breakpoint) pair actually captured for this source.

directives.description: Typed claims parsed from the user's natural-language brief: {axis, source, scope, strength}. axis addresses WHAT is being adopted, source addresses WHOSE reference, scope addresses WHICH subtree (a domPath, or a whole-document sentinel), strength is a [0,1] confidence/weight the parser assigned to the claim.

constraints.description: What must hold post-composition regardless of which sources won which axes: grid integrity, contrast minimums, responsive behavior, and similar invariants that are not themselves a directive but bound what a directive's application is allowed to produce.

conflictResolution.description: Deterministic precedence records. One entry per axis where two or more sources made incompatible claims: the winning source, and (when a specific loser is meaningful) the losing source and what claim it lost. An axis with only a single claimant still gets a trivial entry recording that no contention existed, so this array is never used to silently drop a losing claim -- the loser is always recorded, never just discarded.

provenance.description: Every emitted element/rule traces to a source slot and an evidence pointer. A provenance entry is only meaningful if it RESOLVES: (sourceId, nodeId, domPath, breakpoint) must name a node that was actually captured in that source's snapshot. Attaching an arbitrary sourceId to real-looking coordinates does not resolve.

variantAxes.description: The pre-registered dimensions along which the 3 output variants must structurally differ: layout-skeleton (domPath structure, order-independent), section-order (sequence of sections, order-dependent), motion-timeline (motion signature per element), breakpoint-behavior (how composition varies across breakpoints). Each axis names its own distance metric so 'diverse' cannot be redefined per run.
